variants.title: Run the lifecycle
variants.context: A healthcare AI system moves through five stages: define the use boundary, build traceable evidence, validate the whole workflow, release with containment, then monitor and govern change. Each stage produces the evidence the next stage depends on.
variants.prompt: A hospital wants a sepsis risk score for its emergency department. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Release behind eligibility checks, abstention, human review, versioned outputs, and a tested fallback.
Join outcomes, investigate drift by slice, review overrides and incidents, and revalidate changes.
Control provenance and leakage, separate patients across splits, and document how labels were created.
Test discrimination, calibration, subgroup behavior, usability, and the consequences of errors.
Name the trained user, patient population, setting, input, output, decision, exclusions, and fallback.

variants.hint: Which stage decides who the system is allowed to serve?
variants.explanation: Every later stage is only meaningful against a stated intended use, so the use boundary is written first.

variants.title: Run the lifecycle
variants.context: A healthcare AI system moves through five stages: define the use boundary, build traceable evidence, validate the whole workflow, release with containment, then monitor and govern change. Each stage produces the evidence the next stage depends on.
variants.prompt: A vendor arrives with an already trained chest imaging model and asks the hospital to switch it on next month. Put the work in order.

items.text: Switch it on behind eligibility checks, versioned outputs, and the tested non-AI reading pathway.
Track outcomes, overrides, abstentions, and device mix by slice after go live.
Write the intended use for this site: which patients, which readers, which scanners, and what an abstention means.
Reconstruct the dataset provenance, reference standard, and patient level separation used to build the model.
Evaluate local cases for calibration, subgroup behavior, reading time, and override behavior.

variants.hint: A trained artifact does not skip the earlier stages of the lifecycle.
variants.explanation: An imported model still needs a local intended use and local evidence before it can be released with containment.

variants.title: Run the lifecycle
variants.context: A healthcare AI system moves through five stages: define the use boundary, build traceable evidence, validate the whole workflow, release with containment, then monitor and govern change. Each stage produces the evidence the next stage depends on.
variants.prompt: The records team is replacing the lab unit mapping that feeds a live model, with no change to the weights. Put the work the team must repeat in order.

items.text: Rebuild the evidence for the changed feature, including provenance and label lineage.
Re-release behind eligibility checks, recording the new data contract version and the rollback criterion.
Watch rejected inputs, overrides, and outcomes by slice after the mapping change.
Restate the intended use and check whether the new mapping is still inside the declared input contract.
Revalidate discrimination, calibration, and workflow behavior against the changed input.

variants.hint: A model can leave its validated boundary without its weights changing.
variants.explanation: A data contract change is an evidence question, so the lifecycle runs again from the use boundary.

variants.title: Order the inference path
variants.context: A bounded inference path acquires and identifies the request, checks eligibility, infers and calibrates with a versioned model, presents the result for review in context, then records and observes. The model result never bypasses eligibility, review, or audit.
variants.prompt: A supported request arrives for an eligible patient. Put the stages of the serving path in order.

items.text: Show the basis, limitations, alternatives, and patient context to the intended user.
Return the model version, output, uncertainty or abstention state, and transformation versions.
Bind the source, encounter, device, timestamp, consent, and schema version to the request.
Log the authorized action, override, latency, fallback, and later outcome under the retention policy.
Validate population, setting, modality, quality, required fields, and supported software versions.

variants.hint: What has to be true before a score is even computed?
variants.explanation: Eligibility runs before inference and the audit record closes the path, so no result escapes review.

variants.title: Order the inference path
variants.context: A bounded inference path acquires and identifies the request, checks eligibility, infers and calibrates with a versioned model, presents the result for review in context, then records and observes. The model result never bypasses eligibility, review, or audit.
variants.prompt: A study arrives from a scanner model that is not on the supported list. Put the stages in order, ending with the record.

items.text: The user is shown the approved non-AI pathway and the reason the model did not run.
The system returns an abstention state with its versions instead of a score.
The request is bound to its source, encounter, device model, and acquisition timestamp.
The eligibility check finds a device version outside the validated claim.
The rejected input, reason code, fallback use, and latency are written to the log.

variants.hint: An out of scope input still has to leave a trace.
variants.explanation: Unsupported input is rejected at eligibility and the abstention is recorded like any other decision.

variants.title: Order the inference path
variants.context: A bounded inference path acquires and identifies the request, checks eligibility, infers and calibrates with a versioned model, presents the result for review in context, then records and observes. The model result never bypasses eligibility, review, or audit.
variants.prompt: A new preprocessing release is deployed while the old calibration file is still installed. Put the stages in order, ending with the audit record.

items.text: The version check rejects the mixed preprocessing and calibration contract instead of scoring.
The user sees a visible degraded mode and the ordinary workflow rather than an uncalibrated number.
The version mismatch, incident link, and fallback use are recorded for review.
Eligibility confirms the population, modality, and required fields are in scope.
The request carries its source, encounter, and schema version into the path.

variants.hint: Which check catches a problem that eligibility cannot see?
variants.explanation: Version contracts are checked inside the path, so a mismatch produces a visible fallback rather than a silent number.

variants.title: Do the screening math
variants.context: Sensitivity and specificity are conditional on the true outcome. Prevalence turns them into counts: positive cases times sensitivity are the true positives, negative cases times one minus specificity are the false positives, and the review queue is the sum of the two.
variants.prompt: A screening model runs over 2,000 patients with 5 percent prevalence, at an operating point with 90 percent sensitivity and 92 percent specificity. How many cases land in the review queue?
variants.hint: The queue holds every flagged case, whichever way the truth falls.
variants.explanation: 100 positives times 0.90 gives 90 true positives, 1,900 negatives times 0.08 gives 152 false positives, and the queue is 242.

mistakes.feedback: That counts only the true positives; the queue also carries every false positive.
That is the number of positive cases in the cohort, not the number of flagged results.

variants.title: Do the screening math
variants.context: Sensitivity and specificity are conditional on the true outcome. Prevalence turns them into counts: positive cases times sensitivity are the true positives, negative cases times one minus specificity are the false positives, and the review queue is the sum of the two.
variants.prompt: A cohort of 1,000 patients has 10 percent prevalence. The operating point has 90 percent sensitivity and 90 percent specificity. What percent of the flagged results are true positives?
variants.hint: Divide the true positives by everything the model flagged.
variants.explanation: 90 true positives and 90 false positives make a queue of 180, so half of the flagged results are true.

mistakes.feedback: Sensitivity conditions on the true positives, not on the flagged results.
Prevalence is the share of positives in the cohort, not the share of flags that are correct.

variants.title: Do the screening math
variants.context: Sensitivity and specificity are conditional on the true outcome. Prevalence turns them into counts: positive cases times sensitivity are the true positives, negative cases times one minus specificity are the false positives, and the review queue is the sum of the two.
variants.prompt: The team moves 5,000 patients with 4 percent prevalence to an operating point with 78 percent sensitivity and 98 percent specificity. How many positive cases does the model fail to flag?
variants.hint: Misses come out of the positive cases, not the negative ones.
variants.explanation: 200 positive cases times the 22 percent the model misses gives 44 false negatives, which the ordinary care pathway must still catch.

mistakes.feedback: 156 is the flagged positive count; the question asks how many positives were not flagged.
96 is the false positive count from the 2 percent of negatives, not the missed positives.

variants.title: Fail safely at the boundary
variants.context: Failure behavior has to be explicit. Unsupported input abstains or routes to the approved non-AI workflow, a dependency outage preserves the ordinary workflow in visible degraded mode, and a mixed preprocessing, model, or calibration contract is rejected rather than served.
variants.prompt: A record arrives with a lab unit the model was never validated on, and a helper function could convert it using an assumed factor. What should the serving path do?
options: Convert the value with the assumed factor and score the record.
Score the record and label the output as low confidence.
Abstain and route the record to the approved non-AI workflow.
optionFeedback: A silent coercion invents a data contract that no evidence covers.
A confidence label does not make an ineligible input eligible.
Input outside the validated boundary gets the safe path, not a guess.
variants.hint: Does a label on the output change what the evidence covers?
variants.explanation: Unsupported input is abstained on and routed, because the validated boundary is a runtime check and not a suggestion.

variants.title: Fail safely at the boundary
variants.context: Failure behavior has to be explicit. Unsupported input abstains or routes to the approved non-AI workflow, a dependency outage preserves the ordinary workflow in visible degraded mode, and a mixed preprocessing, model, or calibration contract is rejected rather than served.
variants.prompt: The inference service is unreachable for forty minutes during a busy shift. What should the clinical workflow do?
options: Keep the ordinary workflow running and show that the model is unavailable.
Reuse each patient's most recent cached score from an earlier day.
Hold the affected decisions in a queue until the service returns.
optionFeedback: The ordinary pathway must survive the outage, and degraded mode has to be visible.
A stale score from another day is presented as if it described today's patient.
Holding decisions makes an outage in a support tool block patient care.
variants.hint: What was the workflow doing before the model existed?
variants.explanation: A dependency outage preserves the ordinary workflow and makes degraded mode visible to the user.

variants.title: Fail safely at the boundary
variants.context: Failure behavior has to be explicit. Unsupported input abstains or routes to the approved non-AI workflow, a dependency outage preserves the ordinary workflow in visible degraded mode, and a mixed preprocessing, model, or calibration contract is rejected rather than served.
variants.prompt: Monitoring shows override rates on one site's cases have tripled in two weeks while overall accuracy looks unchanged. What is the right first response?
options: Retrain on the recent data from that site and redeploy.
Investigate that slice and prepare containment while the trigger is open.
Wait for the aggregate metric to move before opening an incident.
optionFeedback: Retraining acts before anyone knows which contract actually broke.
A sharp change in overrides is a predefined incident trigger on its own.
Aggregate accuracy is exactly what hides a single site or population.
variants.hint: Which signal was already declared an incident trigger before release?
variants.explanation: A sharp change in overrides, abstentions, or fallback use is its own trigger, because averages conceal slice level harm.

variants.title: Place the evidence layer
variants.context: Evidence separates into layers: analytical and data validity, model validity, external validity, human factors and workflow validity, and prospective and post-deployment evidence. Each layer answers a different question and no layer substitutes for another.
variants.prompt: Match each evidence layer to the question it answers.

pairs.label: Analytical and data validity
pairs.detail: Verify input integrity, units, acquisition constraints, label quality, and software correctness.

pairs.label: Model validity
pairs.detail: Evaluate discrimination, calibration, uncertainty, and error costs with intervals on untouched data.

pairs.label: External validity
pairs.detail: Test the sites, devices, time periods, and populations that the deployment claim names.

pairs.label: Human factors and workflow validity
pairs.detail: Observe whether intended users understand, challenge, override, and act on outputs as designed.

pairs.label: Prospective and post-deployment evidence
pairs.detail: Use the study design the claim requires, then monitor outcomes and incidents after release.

variants.hint: Ask what each layer would notice that the others cannot.
variants.explanation: No single metric validates a healthcare AI system, so each layer is reported separately against the deployment claim.

variants.title: Place the evidence layer
variants.context: Evidence separates into layers: analytical and data validity, model validity, external validity, human factors and workflow validity, and prospective and post-deployment evidence. Each layer answers a different question and no layer substitutes for another.
variants.prompt: A review finds five problems. Match each one to the evidence layer that should have caught it.

pairs.label: Analytical and data validity
pairs.detail: A unit conversion in the interface silently doubled one lab value for months.

pairs.label: Model validity
pairs.detail: No confidence intervals were ever computed, so a small gap was read as a real improvement.

pairs.label: External validity
pairs.detail: Every evaluation case came from one academic center with one scanner vendor.

pairs.label: Human factors and workflow validity
pairs.detail: Nurses accepted almost every alert without opening the basis panel.

pairs.label: Prospective and post-deployment evidence
pairs.detail: Nobody joined patient outcomes to predictions after go live.

variants.hint: Each failure has one layer whose job it was.
variants.explanation: Layers fail independently, so a gap in one cannot be argued away with strong results from another.

variants.title: Place the evidence layer
variants.context: Evidence separates into layers: analytical and data validity, model validity, external validity, human factors and workflow validity, and prospective and post-deployment evidence. Each layer answers a different question and no layer substitutes for another.
variants.prompt: A second review finds five more problems. Match each one to the evidence layer it belongs to.

pairs.label: Analytical and data validity
pairs.detail: Three scans from the same patient were split across development and test data.

pairs.label: Model validity
pairs.detail: Ranking stayed strong while predicted probabilities drifted far from observed rates.

pairs.label: External validity
pairs.detail: Performance fell at a rural site running older acquisition devices.

pairs.label: Human factors and workflow validity
pairs.detail: Clinicians overrode most alerts and then stopped reading them at all.

pairs.label: Prospective and post-deployment evidence
pairs.detail: An adverse event was reported and no one could say which model version ran.

variants.hint: Ask which stage of the evidence path each symptom belongs to.
variants.explanation: Slice, calibration, workflow, and post-release evidence are distinct claims, so each has to be tested on its own layer.
